artifacts.summary: 8-phase implementation of the postflight completion-deploy gate: shared freshness library, check-only exit-6 backstop in update-task-status.sh, regression suite, two serialized baseline-relative deploy triggers, the mandatory carve-out, and a deployed, dogfooded self-demonstration.

completion_data.completion_summary: Implemented a check-only, unconditional postflight completion-deploy gate (exit 6) in update-task-status.sh that refuses a source-store-touching task's completion while its deploy is provably stale, with two serialized baseline-relative redeploy triggers (single-task and multi-task paths), the mandatory carve-out in regeneration-is-manual-only.md, and a shared deploy-freshness-lib.sh backing both the new blocking tier and the pre-existing advisory check. Deployed and dogfooded against this task's own completion.

memory_candidates.content: When a bash script needs to `source` scripts/lib/file-scope-overlap.sh under `set -e`, use `if ! . "$LIB" 2>/dev/null; then ...; fi`, never a bare `. "$LIB"`. That library's FILE_SCOPE_OVERLAP_JQ_DEFS assignment uses `read -r -d '' ... <<'JQDEFS'`, which returns exit 1 at heredoc EOF even on a fully successful read (a documented bash `read -d ''` quirk) -- a bare source trips `set -e` and aborts the whole calling script right there. task-lock.sh's own `ensure_file_scope_overlap_lib` already guards this way; mirror it rather than debugging a mysterious abort.

A new script added under agent-system/extensions/<ext>/scripts/** (or scripts/lib/**, scripts/tests/**) is invisible to deploy-headless.sh until it is also added to that extension's manifest.json `provides.scripts` array. Without that registration, check-extension-docs.sh reports 'script file on disk NOT in provides.scripts' and the file is never copied to the deployed .claude/ tree on redeploy -- a silent gap that only surfaces later as a byte-diff or a missing-file test failure. When a plan's file_scope lists a NEW script file, manifest.json registration is an implicit, necessary companion edit even if the plan's own file_scope list omits it.

deploy-headless.sh resyncs the WHOLE deployed tree (every loaded extension), not just the extension a given task edited. Running it while a concurrent sibling session has uncommitted or freshly-committed changes in a DIFFERENT extension will sweep those changes into the deploy too, and a subsequent verify-deploy.sh --findings diff will show findings for files that task never touched. Before treating a post-deploy finding as a regression introduced by your own task, check whether the finding's file is inside your own file_scope -- if not, it is very likely collateral from a concurrent session's own in-flight work, not a defect in what you built.
